statement: The function returns a result r and the sequence of elements of r equals the inorder sequence of root. Define inorder(t) recursively: inorder(Null) = [] and inorder(Node(v, l, r)) = inorder(l) ++ [v] ++ inorder(r). Then len(r) = len(inorder(root)) and for every i with 0 <= i < len(r), r[i] = (inorder(root))[i].
preconditions: The number of nodes in root is between 0 and 100 inclusive, and every node value v satisfies -100 <= v <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) equals the number of nodes in root, where the number of nodes is defined by nodes(Null) = 0 and nodes(Node(v, l, r)) = 1 + nodes(l) + nodes(r).
preconditions: None (the property holds for every tree).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer x, the number of occurrences of x in r equals the number of nodes in root whose value is x.
preconditions: The number of nodes in root is between 0 and 100 inclusive, and every node value v satisfies -100 <= v <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every index i with 0 <= i < len(r), -100 <= r[i] <= 100.
preconditions: The number of nodes in root is between 0 and 100 inclusive, and every node value v satisfies -100 <= v <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) > 0, and r[0] equals the value of the leftmost node of root (the node reached by starting at root and repeatedly taking the left child until there is no left child), and r[len(r)-1] equals the value of the rightmost node of root (the node reached by starting at root and repeatedly taking the right child until there is no right child).
preconditions: root ≠ Null and the tree satisfies the problem constraints: at most 100 nodes and every node value v with -100 <= v <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the sequence of elements of r equals inorder(L) ++ [v] ++ inorder(R), where inorder is the standard inorder sequence (inorder(Null)=[]; inorder(Node(w, a, b))=inorder(a)++[w]++inorder(b)).
preconditions: root = Node(v, L, R) for some value v and subtrees L and R; the tree satisfies the problem constraints.

statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail).
preconditions: The number of nodes in root is between 0 and 100 inclusive.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the elements of r are exactly the values along the unique right-descending path from root to the deepest node, in order from root to leaf. If root = Null, r is empty.
preconditions: Every node in root has no left child (i.e., for every node, its left subtree is Null); the tree satisfies the problem constraints.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the elements of r are exactly the values along the unique left-descending path from root to the deepest node, in order from deepest to root. If root = Null, r is empty.
preconditions: Every node in root has no right child (i.e., for every node, its right subtree is Null); the tree satisfies the problem constraints.

statement: Define inorder(Null) = [] and inorder(Node(w, A, B)) = inorder(A) ++ [w] ++ inorder(B). Whenever the function returns Ok r, for every subtree occurrence Node(w, L, R) of root there exist sequences P and Q such that r = P ++ inorder(L) ++ [w] ++ inorder(R) ++ Q.
preconditions: The tree root satisfies the problem constraints: 0 <= nodes(root) <= 100 and every node value v satisfies -100 <= v <= 100.
